newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST - NZ$18-20 mln profit seen for Sky.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - NZ$18-20 mln profit seen for Sky.

text.p: Analysts expect casino group Sky City to report a net profit of around NZ$18-20 million in the first half to December but with considerable potential for improvement in the second half.
Sky City made a NZ$15.5 million net profit in its first five months of operation to June 30, 1996 and is due to report for the half-year to December on Monday.
One analyst expected NZ$17.5-18 million, for a full year profit of NZ$38 million, comfortably ahead of offer document forecasts but at the lower end of most brokers' expectations.
Income from gaming was expected to be strong but analysts said the peripheral activities had been slow to get off the ground.
Raymond Webb at ANZ Securities expects a net profit of NZ$17-20 million, a full year profit of NZ$36-40 million, and for the gaming operation to outperform expectations.
"Unfortunately most of that will be lost due to a very poor performance from the peripheral operations, particuarly from the bars, restaurants, carparks and the theatre," he said.
The non-casino activities were all high fixed-cost businesses where to date Sky City had not quite got the positioning right to attract sufficient customers, he said.
"Going forward, I would expect the gaming operation to perform very strongly and as they start to get peripheral operations on track, that that could give quite an uplift to earnings," he said.
Sky City's hotel occupancy is running at about 75 percent, against prospectus forecasts of 83 percent and compared to the average for Auckland of 73.7.

Sky City is half-owned by Brierley Investments Ltd. Harrah's Entertainment, which manages the casino, owns 12.5 percent. The company's listing documents forecast a NZ$35.8 million profit for the year to June 1997 -- its first full year of trading -- and $40.8 million in 1997-8.
